solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spike and Sam somehow say the wrong thing (8)

indicators.note: the letters are put together in some other way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters; 'and' just joins the two names

annotation.surface: Two people called Spike and Sam have somehow put their feet in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals dress Spike and Sam up as people; to the solver they are just eight letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the prefix mis- means wrongly, so this is speaking wrongly, a slip of the tongue.

clue.text: Manage to cook on occasion (4,2)

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: to cook a meal is to make it
a do is a party or social occasion

annotation.surface: Someone manages to do some cooking now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On occasion' reads as one phrase meaning sometimes, but it splits: 'on' is a placing instruction and 'occasion' is a party.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to get by with whatever is to hand is to manage.

clue.text: Curse drunk old women’s drawers (9)

indicators.note: a drunk's letters are in no fit state, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
W is the standard abbreviation for women; the apostrophe-s just links it to the next word
anagram fodder, taken as printed

annotation.surface: A curse is laid on drunk old women's underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: The drawers look like knickers, but they are just seven letters to mix with the two single letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a curse is a profane word, an oath.

clue.text: Subject of medicine rarely studied to begin with (7)

indicators.note: the word for medicine is one now rarely used
take only the opening letter

blocks.note: physic is an old-fashioned word for medicine
first letter of studied

annotation.surface: A medical subject that hardly anyone studies at first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' seems to go with 'studied', but it belongs to medicine: it flags an archaic word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: it is one school or university subject among many.

clue.text: Severe wound in casualty department (5)

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department
a cut is a wound; it goes inside A…E

annotation.surface: A badly wounded patient is brought into the emergency room.
annotation.walkthrough: A&E (Accident and Emergency) is what British hospitals call the emergency room; the ampersand drops out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as of an illness or shortage that is intense and serious.

clue.text: Taken unawares, general bitten by snake (6)

definitions.note: 'Taken unawares' is used in the sense of caught napping, off guard

indicators.note: the snake's jaws close around the general

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general; he goes inside AS…P

annotation.surface: A general is caught by surprise when a snake bites him.
annotation.walkthrough: The American Civil War general Robert E. Lee is the crossword's favourite general.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose sense: someone caught napping is off guard, not alert to what is coming.

clue.text: Way in which drunken hobos might be viewed? (4,3)

definitions.text: Way in which drunken hobos might be viewed?

blocks.note: the surface reads a manner, how they are seen; the setter means a road, a street
a street where down-and-outs are a common sight

annotation.surface: A question about how society looks at drunken tramps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Way' reads as manner, but it is a literal street: skid row is the run-down district of drifters and drunks.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the phrase names a run-down street, a way, where vagrants gather.

clue.text: Report of school getting demolished (5)

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so go by sound

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English boarding school

annotation.surface: News that a school is being knocked down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Demolished' suggests buildings, but here it is food: a demolished meal is all gone.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: to demolish a plate of food is to wolf it all down.

clue.text: Truly gripping spectacles? (5-3)

blocks.note: the surface means thrilling; the setter means literally holding on tight
not shows or sights but glasses

annotation.surface: A rave review of a thrilling show or sight.
annotation.walkthrough: The name is French for 'pinch nose': glasses with no arms that stay on by clipping the bridge of the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: these glasses really do grip, by pinching the nose.

clue.text: Killer dope entertaining soldiers one November (8)

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in

blocks.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
the Special Air Service, British special forces; they go inside AS…S
I is the Roman numeral one
N is November in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A deadly drug is being given to soldiers and someone in November.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' first suggests drugs, and 'Killer dope' a lethal one; the dope is a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for one who kills a prominent person.

clue.text: Don’t get so excited and don’t go topless! (4,4,5,2)

blocks.note: an informal plea to calm down
the same idiom taken literally: stay dressed on top

annotation.surface: Someone tells an overexcited friend to calm down and stay dressed.
annotation.walkthrough: The same phrase does both jobs: the idiom for calm down, and its literal sense.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for calm down, whose literal sense is to stay covered above the waist.

clue.text: Accommodation, initially in church, for those needing winter quarters (7)

indicators.note: what comes initially in a word is its opening letter, so only the I of 'in' is used

blocks.note: a dorm, dormitory, is shared sleeping accommodation
first letter of in
CE is the Church of England

annotation.surface: A church offers lodging to people who need somewhere to stay over winter.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a winter night shelter for the homeless; the ones needing winter quarters are hibernating animals.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by habit: these small rodents hibernate for months, so they need a snug winter nest.

clue.text: Order phoned in a long time back (7)

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the era is read from its end

blocks.note: an era is a long time; turned round it gives ARE
rang = phoned; it goes inside AR…E

annotation.surface: An order was placed by telephone ages ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' could be a command or a purchase; here it is a verb, to put in order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to put things in order, to sort them.

clue.text: One in Rolls makes merry (8)

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: rolls are lists of names, rosters
I is the Roman numeral one; it goes inside RO…STERS

annotation.surface: Someone riding in a Rolls-Royce is living it up.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital R makes 'Rolls' look like the car; it is lists, as in a roll call.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to celebrate noisily and boisterously.

clue.text: Train company tours are flexible (8)

indicators.note: flexible letters can bend into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A rail operator's trips can be booked with flexible dates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Are' does double duty: it is part of the fodder and completes the indicator's grammar.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: the operator running trains through the Channel Tunnel between London and the Continent.

clue.text: Partners grabbing most of wine? Rubbish! (5)

indicators.note: the outer piece takes hold of the inner one
most of something is all but a little of it, so the wine loses just its final letter

blocks.note: West and East are partners at bridge
Asti, the Italian sparkling wine, minus its last letter; it goes inside W…E

annotation.surface: A couple reach for the bottle, and someone thinks it is rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: At bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, and West partners East.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: material thrown away as useless.

clue.text: Maybe Dolly’s relations hide from her (9)

blocks.note: Dolly, the cloned sheep, is one example of a sheep, so a sheep's
kin are relatives

annotation.surface: Dolly's family members are hiding from her.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb in the surface; it is a noun, an animal's skin, and 'from her' points back to Dolly.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by origin: the hide that comes from an animal like Dolly, fleece and all.

clue.text: Paparazzo may take one or two photographs (8)

indicators.note: asks for two different words for photographs, one after the other

blocks.note: a snap is a photograph
a shot is also a photograph

annotation.surface: A press photographer might grab a picture or two.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One or two photographs' reads as a vague number; it splits, with 'one' ending the definition and 'two' asking for a pair of synonyms.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a quick candid picture is exactly what a paparazzo grabs.

clue.text: Backing for one horse — might it encourage you? (5)

definitions.note: the definition describes the thing as a noun; the answer is also the verb for encourage

indicators.note: the whole piece runs backwards

blocks.note: e.g., for example, is 'for one'
a dun is a greyish-brown horse

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether betting on a single horse might spur you on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' tempts you toward betting on the horse; it is the reversal instruction for the whole string.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: a gentle push with the elbow is meant to encourage someone to act.

clue.text: Leader avoiding most demanding summit (7)

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: the most demanding is the severest
the leading S is removed

annotation.surface: A leader stays away from the hardest of summit meetings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a meeting of leaders, which is why 'Leader' fits the surface so snugly.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the world's highest mountain top.

clue.text: Design of new drone acclaimed (8)

indicators.note: the letters are designed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A new drone's design has won praise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New' is easy to read as an anagram indicator; here it is fodder, and 'Design of' does the mixing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: famous and widely praised.

clue.text: Soldier fighting with Resistance capturing city (7)

indicators.note: the outer piece takes the inner one prisoner

blocks.note: war is fighting
Rio de Janeiro; it goes inside WAR…R
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

annotation.surface: A soldier fighting alongside the Resistance takes a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fighting with Resistance' together forms the outer piece, which then captures the city.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fighter, especially one of old.

clue.text: Band stand still, some would say (6)

indicators.note: spoken by some, so go by sound

blocks.note: to freeze is to stand stock-still

annotation.surface: A pop group on stage is told not to move.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' and 'stand' conjure musicians and a bandstand; the band is a decorative strip along a wall.
annotation.definitionFit: An architectural sense: a horizontal decorative strip running along a wall.

clue.text: Have gangs of youths succeeded? (7)

blocks.note: a posse is a gang, especially of youngsters
S is short for succeeded, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A question about whether youth gangs have won.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have' opens the clue like an auxiliary verb; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to own or hold.

clue.text: Frenchman embroiled in impressive battle (5)

indicators.note: caught up inside the other piece

blocks.note: as in 'that was some party', meaning impressive
M is Monsieur; it goes inside SO…ME

annotation.surface: A Frenchman is caught up in a great battle.
annotation.walkthrough: The battle was fought in northern France, so the Frenchman is at home in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 1916 First World War battle named after a French river.

clue.text: Violinist quite unlike Yehudi Menuhin, an abrasive sort (7)

blocks.note: Menuhin was a virtuoso; his opposite is a poor fiddler who grates the bow across the strings
not a rude person but a tool that rubs a surface away

annotation.surface: An unkind review of a violinist who plays nothing like Menuhin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abrasive sort' sounds like a rude person but is a tool.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb scrape: a bad violinist, and a tool for scraping.

clue.text: Died in heavenly city that was built by the Phoenicians (5)

definitions.text: city that was built by the Phoenicians

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Sion, or Zion, is the heavenly city of Jerusalem
D is short for died; it goes inside SI…ON

annotation.surface: Someone died in paradise, a city the Phoenicians built.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'city' twice over: once in the heavenly city of the wordplay and once in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by history: an ancient Phoenician port, in what is now Lebanon.

clue.text: Tools meeting standard of old (6,3,6)

blocks.note: two tools, one for the factory worker and one for the farmer
a standard is a flag; this was the emblem of the former Soviet Union

annotation.surface: Tools that meet an old-fashioned standard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as a benchmark but is a flag; 'meeting' also suits the crossed tools on that flag.
annotation.definitionFit: Two tools, and the crossed pair that was the Soviet flag's emblem.

clue.text: Two votes for this cardinal (6)

blocks.note: a vote is marked with a cross, X; two crosses make XX in Roman numerals
not a churchman at a papal election but a cardinal number

annotation.surface: A church cardinal wins a couple of votes, as in a papal election.
annotation.walkthrough: The cardinal is not a churchman but a counting number; a vote is marked X, and XX is twenty.
annotation.definitionFit: A mathematical sense: cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, and XX is one of them.

clue.text: Approach as femme fatale undoubtedly will? (8)

blocks.note: a noun: the way in to a building or drive
a verb: what a seductress does to her victims, putting them under a spell

annotation.surface: A question about how a seductress walks into a room.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but said differently: EN-trance, a way in, and en-TRANCE, to captivate.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun for a way in and a verb for bewitch, spelt the same but stressed differently.
